Precondition: A Good LOT at a known location
Step: Move the LOT to a new location
Expected Result: An immutable LotMovement row records LOT, from-location, to-location, moved-by user, terminal, and timestamp; CurrentLocationId is updated

Precondition: A LOT that has been moved
Step: Open the LOT history
Expected Result: The movement appears in the LOT history with the timestamp in Eastern time

Precondition: A dedicated terminal with an operator presence established
Step: Scan a LOT on the Movement Scan screen and record the move
Expected Result: Destination defaults to the terminal's parent location (read-only); LOT is looked up by LTT, validated not Closed, and the move is recorded and confirmed

Precondition: A LOT whose item is not eligible at the chosen destination
Step: Attempt the validated move
Expected Result: System rejects the move — the item must resolve at the destination (or an ancestor tier)
Notes: Already-at-this-location is pre-checked and the Move action is disabled

Precondition: A LOT that has already advanced past an operation step
Step: Attempt to move it back to that earlier operation
Expected Result: Backward move is blocked with a message; a supervisor-override affordance permits it when authorized

Precondition: A LOT on Hold or Closed
Step: Attempt to move the LOT
Expected Result: System refuses to move a blocked or closed LOT

Precondition: A component LOT (Die Cast / Trim / intermediate Machining) ready to advance
Step: Use the combined Complete + Move action
Expected Result: Status transition and movement happen in one atomic action; a partial basket is only Closed when the operator closes it

Precondition: An assembly finished-goods LOT filling a shipping container
Step: Complete the container
Expected Result: The associated finished-goods LOT auto-closes as part of the Container Complete transaction

Precondition: A LOT started with N pieces at a workstation
Step: Complete a partial quantity M (M less than or equal to N) later
Expected Result: Start and Complete are independent operations with independent quantities, valid across shift boundaries
Notes: Verify at MVP: current build records checkpoint/flexible-operator quantities on the FIFO consume path rather than separate Start/Complete fields — confirm against this requirement

Precondition: Start/Complete/Scrap events recorded for a LOT
Step: Review the derived in-process quantity
Expected Result: In-process quantity is derived by event replay rather than a running atomic counter

Precondition: A partially-progressed LOT at a Cell
Step: Pause the LOT to work another LOT at the same Cell
Expected Result: An open PauseEvent is written; the paused LOT keeps its partial state and the operator can run other LOTs at that Cell
Notes: Pause is orthogonal to LOT status — no Paused status row

Precondition: A Cell with one or more open pauses
Step: Tap the Paused-LOT indicator and resume a LOT from the list
Expected Result: Indicator shows the open-pause count; selecting and confirming resumes via LotPause_Resume and records ResumedByUserId (may differ from the pauser)
Notes: No auto-prompt to resume; no TTL

Precondition: A blocked LOT and a LOT already paused at a Cell
Step: Attempt to pause a held/closed LOT and to open a second pause at the same Cell
Expected Result: Blocked/closed LOT cannot be paused; at most one open pause per (LOT, location) is enforced

Precondition: A container with a shipping label at the Shipping Dock
Step: Scan the container's shipping label
Expected Result: System validates the container is Complete (not Hold/Void/already Shipped) and the label is not void before loading

Precondition: A container that is on hold / void / not Complete
Step: Scan the label at the dock
Expected Result: System prevents loading and displays the reason

Precondition: A valid Complete container with a non-void label
Step: Confirm the ship
Expected Result: Container status flips to Shipped, it moves to the shipping-out location, and the event is logged to Audit.OperationLog
Notes: Container has no source LotId — traceability is the container's own location move + ContainerShipped audit, not a per-LOT LotMovement

Precondition: A held container of serialized parts sent to the Sort Cage
Step: Unpack and re-pack a good serialized part into a new open container
Expected Result: ContainerSerial is updated to the new container/tray position (SortCage_MigrateSerial); the destination container must be Open

Precondition: A serial migrated at the Sort Cage
Step: Review the migration record
Expected Result: A ContainerSerialHistory row captures old/new container and tray position, migration reason, and migrated-by user

Precondition: A re-sort producing new LOTs and re-packed containers
Step: Verify the downstream label and AIM steps fire
Expected Result: New LTT labels (reason SORT_CAGE), new shipping labels, voiding of old labels, and AIM UpdateAim for serial migrations occur
Notes: Commissioning/partially-unwired: confirm which side-effects (new-LTT/label print, old-label void, AIM UpdateAim) are actually wired — the migrate-serial proc updates ContainerSerial only; label + AIM fan-out may be commissioning-time

Precondition: A Sort Cage disposition
Step: Disposition good vs bad parts
Expected Result: Disposition uses holds, splits, scrap, and re-pack; no formal NCM disposition codes or rework routing are surfaced (FUTURE)

Workflow: Sort cage is not a merge
Precondition: A serialized part migrated from a held container into a new container
Step: Inspect genealogy after the migration
Expected Result: No LotGenealogy merge record is created; SerializedPart.LotId still points to the original source LOT (traceability preserved through the serial)

Precondition: A defective part identified during Sort Cage inspection
Step: Disposition the defective part
Expected Result: Scrap follows the split-to-scrap workflow (a Split genealogy record), never a Merge record
